findings.title: Preserve the watched-reconcile gate before arming
findings.description: The weekly command can finish successfully while unarmed; in that case it logs a “done (unarmed)” line without running the destructive offsite mirror. This code accepts that line and immediately creates `RECONCILE-ARMED`, enabling future cron runs to sync and purge offsite data without the required watched reconcile. Keep the arm file absent until the armed reconcile has been performed and observed. The current `test_weekly_success_arms` test also codifies arming after an unarmed run.

findings.title: Reject lifecycle rules that hide current objects
findings.description: The lifecycle check accepts a rule based only on its prefix and `daysFromHidingToDeleting`. It does not check that `daysFromUploadingToHiding` is unset, as the runbook requires. A rule that hides objects after 30 days and deletes them 30 days later would therefore be reported as OK, even though it can hide current backups from the live prefix. Validate that no applicable rule hides current objects before reporting OK.

findings.title: Verify the health command succeeded and produced a fresh result
findings.description: `run_health` discards the result of `shell()` and trusts the last line in the health log. If the command fails before appending a new log entry, an older healthy `FLAGS` line can be treated as the current result, allowing the cutover to proceed on stale health data. Require a successful command and verify the log entry belongs to that invocation.
